lines.text: Centuries ago, there was no king—only an ordinary piece of firewood.
One day, the wood found itself inside an old carpenter's shop.
The carpenter was called Mastro Cherry because of his round, red nose.
Delighted with the wood, he decided to turn it into a table leg.
As he lifted his hatchet, a tiny voice begged him to be careful.
Mastro Cherry froze and searched the room, but he found nobody.
Convinced that he had imagined it, he returned to his work.
The moment he struck the wood, the voice cried out in pain.
His eyes widened, and fear left him unable to speak.
Could an ordinary piece of firewood really cry like a child?
He grabbed the log and knocked it against the floor and walls.
When the room stayed silent, he tried to laugh away his fear.
Then his plane made the wood giggle because it tickled.
Shocked beyond words, Mastro Cherry collapsed onto the floor.
